name: Channels REST API (bind, unbind, list, test, groups)
description:
## Context
Follow the REST conventions already used in this project (see the profiles/knowledge endpoints): identity lives in the URL/query (`project_id` as a query param), bodies only describe the resource, `PUT` = upsert, `DELETE` takes the resource name/id as a query param, and a single `Depends` chain validates project + permissions (403/404) once per request.

## Objective
Expose channel bindings over HTTP.

## Steps
1. `codx/junior/api/channels.py` (extend the file created for the webhook):
   - `GET /api/channels?project_id=` → bindings + WhatsApp status (enabled, phone number, verify token configured: bool, sdk version).
   - `PUT /api/channels?project_id=` → upsert a binding (`ChannelBindingUpsert` body); admin only; `ValueError` from the store → HTTP 400 with the message verbatim.
   - `DELETE /api/channels?project_id=&binding_id=` → remove a binding; admin only.
   - `POST /api/channels/{binding_id}/test?project_id=` → send a test message to the external conversation, return the Meta response or the error.
   - `GET /api/channels/whatsapp/groups?project_id=` → list WhatsApp groups known to the business number.
   - `POST /api/channels/whatsapp/groups?project_id=` → create a group (`subject`, `participants`) and return the binding.
2. Reuse `require_admin` / `get_current_session` from `codx/junior/api/__init__.py`; check project access through `UserSecurityManager`.
3. Request models: `ConfigDict(str_strip_whitespace=True)` with explicit bounds on `external_id` / `meta` strings.

## Files
- codx/junior/api/channels.py
- codx/junior/app.py (router already registered by the webhook task)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Bind / unbind / list / test work end to end from the API docs.
- [ ] Non-admin gets 403 on write endpoints; a user without project access gets 403/404.
- [ ] Invalid/duplicate binding returns 400 with a readable message.
- [ ] Endpoints visible in `/api/docs`.
